definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

mustMatch: 4 diagonal overlapping slashes with raised ears and recessed crumb
crumb colour never bleeds outside the slash trenches

niceToHave: exact slash tilt angle (a visual estimate, not measured)

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Both tips are true poles (radius -> 0); no underside geometry exists to hide, so the harness's flat-lit shadowless render has nothing to occlude there.
The harness normalizes the longest axis to 1.6, so absolute dimensions are arbitrary and only the authored ratios carry meaning.
Exact slash tilt angle is a visual estimate (32deg), not an independently measured value - accepted like pancake's unmeasured pore positions.

coordinateFrame.front: +X is the length axis; the harness three-quarter camera sits at (-1.6, 2.2, 2.6)
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: cross-section radius = 1.0 relative unit. Absolute scale is meaningless: the consumer runtime refits the longest axis to 1.6 (scripts/breads/types.ts section 7).

componentTree.name: Tapered crust shell
componentTree.topologyRationale: A single continuous tube swept along the length axis with a radius profile tapering to true poles at both ends - genuinely a tapered sweep, not a lathe (LatheGeometry is banned per CRIB: phi-seam vertex duplication tears under jitter).

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: low-poly prop, faceted after generation, highest facet density of the chunk group

latheProfile.note: Not a lathe - swept along X through hand-authored STATIONS (radius(x)), true poles at both tips. See scripts/breads/baguette.ts.

deformationStack.notes: Grid-cell classification generalized from scone's point-fissure and loaf's ridge-sweep techniques to a 2D oriented band on an unrolled tube surface. For each (station, sector) grid vertex near the top of the tube, its local (X, arc-length-from-top) position is rotated by -32deg into the slash's own (along, across) frame; if |along| < halfLength and |across| < widthEnvelope(along) (an elliptical eye-shaped envelope that closes to 0 at along=+-halfLength) the vertex is inside the slash footprint. Vertices in the inner ~55% of the width envelope are the crumb-coloured trench floor (dipped inward); the outer band is the raised crust-coloured ear (pushed outward). Triangles are classified crumb by majority vertex vote, then emitted in two ordered passes (crust triangles first, then crumb) so scripts/breads/lib.ts sliceTriangles can split them by a single contiguous boundary index, exactly like scone's body/face split - generalized here from a single shared ring to four independent oriented bands scattered across the grid.

featureReviews.notes: Extreme tapered-spindle silhouette reads correctly, both tips close to true poles, no holes anywhere (winding verified analytically pre-render via check_winding.py, catching the exact bug loaf hit empirically - a 50/50 split where each quad's two triangles need INDEPENDENT winding, not a naive 'flip both together'). L/D measured at 11.365 via PIL pixel bbox on baguette-2.png (image-analysis.json, not eyeballed). bilateralSymmetryError 0.104 is the best of the four chunk/hero breads so far (loaf 0.22-0.24, scone 0.19), evidence the true 3D shape is well-formed. Tier1 aspect-ratio delta 0.373 is elevated versus pancake/scone/loaf's residuals; the reference is composed diagonally across a square frame specifically because of this extreme aspect ratio, while the harness's fixed camera shows an X-aligned object at whatever angle it naturally falls - a framing/composition difference, not a shape defect, per grimoire's own caveat on procedural-vs-AI-render pixel-aligned signals.

4 diagonal slashes, evenly spaced, tilted 32deg from the length axis, visibly overlapping - matches the reference's count and general diagonal-overlap pattern. Took 6 render iterations to get here: v1-v2 (shallow depth) read as tiny scattered marks; v3 (more stations) barely helped; v4 (more segments) revealed the real bottleneck was slash WIDTH not resolution - the trench was a thin checkmark, not a lens; v5 widened it correctly but then along-axis resolution became the limiter again (chevron-stepped edges); v6 raised station density once more. Final shape reads as 4 connected diagonal lens marks but with a visibly jagged/spiky top edge rather than the reference's smooth eye boundary - an acceptable low-poly roughness given this is now firmly a resolution-vs-budget tradeoff, not an unresolved mechanism bug.

Cream crumb colour visible inside each slash, clearly contrasting the crust; raised ear band (EAR_RAISE 0.11) is present in the geometry (check_slash_coverage.py: 6-13 ear cells per slash) but reads more subtly than the reference's very bright, sharply-lit ear rim - the harness's ambient-heavy lighting is less forgiving of a shallow raised feature than the reference's own render.
No authored shadow or dark patch under either tip - the harness is flat-lit and shadowless by construction (same as every other bread), automatically satisfying this.
Highest facet density of the chunk group (2048 tri vs scone's 396 / loaf's 260), matching the reference's visibly denser low-poly facet field. Flat shading baked via facet() throughout.

visualEvidence.notes: diagnose_render blockout (aligned): silhouetteIoU=0.5281, aspectRatioDelta=0.3734, scaleDelta=0.2872, bilateralSymmetryError=0.1044, colorDelta.maxDeltaE=27.68. diagnose_render_multi_angle: 2/4 false-positive DEGENERATE (verified non-empty via direct pixel sampling, documented above).

Stopping here - further iteration on the framing-driven tier1 deltas would not fix a model defect, and slash smoothness is now a budget tradeoff, not an open mechanism bug.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Hard cap 8000tri/250KB. Target band for the chunk group (scone/loaf/baguette) is 800-1500tri/<=160KB - baguette is the densest of the three (highest facet count observed in the reference, plus 4 independent slash zones needing angular resolution), so it should land near the top of that band, unlike loaf's deliberately sparse 260tri.

lightingFromPhoto.exposure: no exposure control, no tone mapping.

lightingFromPhoto.contactShadow: none - matches the reference's explicit 'no dark patch under either tapered end' instruction.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Cool directional fill, low intensity, opposite the key.
lightingFromPhoto.toneMapping: NoToneMapping; no AO on the runtime material.

proceduralStrategy: Sweep a circular cross-section along X through hand-authored STATIONS (radius(x)), dense in the slash-bearing middle, sparse in the smooth taper zones, true poles at both tips.

Classify each (station, sector) grid vertex against 4 oriented slash footprints (rotated local along/across coordinates on the unrolled tube surface) - dip the inner trench band, raise the outer ear band.
Jitter vertices while indexed, so shared vertices move together and no face tears open.
Bake faceting by splitting vertices and recomputing normals; never request flatShading.
Project cylindrical UVs along X, then merge by material into exactly two meshes (crust triangles first, crumb triangles emitted after via ordered classification, then split with sliceTriangles).
animationAnchors: root pivot supports whole-object rotation for the showcase turntable
destructionAnchors: single rigid body; no plausible sub-fracture for a baked good this size

risks.description: Any vertex-colour region paint is discarded by the runtime Lambert swap.
risks.mitigation: Two-tone split carried by two separate materials, split on classified grid geometry.

risks.description: flatShading is not inherited by the runtime swap.
risks.mitigation: Faceting baked into geometry via lib.ts facet() before export.

risks.description: Body and slash floors share vertices; jittering independently would tear the seam.
risks.mitigation: Build one indexed tube geometry, jitter it whole, classify and reorder triangles only after.

risks.description: A slash trench narrower than the sector's angular spacing lands between vertices and disappears silently (bit pancake's pores and scone's first fissure attempt).
risks.mitigation: SEGMENTS chosen (22) so the slash half-width (0.26 radius units) spans at least ~2 sectors at the tube's circumference; verified analytically before rendering in check_slash_coverage.py.

risks.description: pancake's (cos t, y, sin t) winding note assumes a Y-axis lathe; sweeping along X instead changes which triangle vertex order faces outward (loaf hit this: an inward-facing tube and, separately, an inward-facing end cap).
risks.mitigation: Winding verified analytically (face-normal dot outward-vector check) for both the tube and both pole fans before the first render, reusing loaf's check_cap_winding.py pattern.

risks.description: mergeByMaterial throws when geometries in one bucket carry different attribute sets.
risks.mitigation: Every geometry gets exactly position, normal and uv; no color attribute is ever created.
